english.title: Shipper contravene requirements of Reg 11(1) re preparation of goods for transport
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a shipper, offered packaged goods, namely **(..SPECIFY GOODS..) for carriage when

(A)_[all the conditions specified in the IMDG Code had not been complied with in relation to their declaration, classification, marking, packaging, labelling, placarding and prior notification to competent authority or consignee]_
(B)_[the goods being in a portable tank, had not been properly and safely prepared for carriage by sea by complying with applicable tank requirements in accordance with the IMDG Code]_
(C)_[the goods being in a tank container, had not been properly and safely prepared for carriage by sea by complying with applicable tank requirements in accordance with the IMDG Code]_
(D)_[the goods being in a vehicle, had not been properly and safely prepared for carriage by sea by complying with applicable tank requirements in accordance with the IMDG Code]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 11(4) and 24(1) of the Merchant Shipping (Dangerous Goods and Marine Pollutants) Regulations 1997.

english.notes:
In proceedings for an offence under this section, it shall be a defence for a person to prove that

(a) all reasonable steps had been taken by him to ensure compliance with the regulations; or
(b) he did not know nor ought to have known nor had reasonable grounds for suspecting the goods to be dangerous goods or marine pollutants as the case may be; or
(c) that the goods were carried and handled in accordance with the provisions of the IMDG code where appropriate; or
(d) if the person charged is the operator or master, in the case of goods packed in a freight container or vehicle, that before the freight container or vehicle was taken on board the ship the person responsible for packing the goods into the freight container of vehicle had provided the operator or master of the ship with a signed packing certificate certifying that the goods had been properly packed in the freight container or vehicle; or
(e) the goods being solid dangerous goods in bulk were being handled and carried in accordance with the IMSBC Code; or
(f) the goods being liquid or gaseous dangerous goods in bulk such goods were being handled and carried in accordance with the relevant requirements of the BCH Code, the IBC Code, the Gas Carrier Code, the Gas Carrier Code for Existing Ships or the IGC Code;
(g) the goods were being carried in accordance with Merchant Shipping Notices MSN 1705 or MSN 1706 where appropriate.

Regulation 24(2)
